# 1 Enoch Chapter 102 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Ge'ez MS; cf. 4QEn (Aramaic) | **Section:** Epistle of Enoch

---

**1** In those days, when he brings a scorching fire down on you — where will you run? Where will you find safety? And when he speaks against you — won't you shudder with fear?

**2** Every light in the sky will be seized with terror. The whole earth will be afraid, will tremble, will shake with alarm.

**3** Even the angels will follow their orders while trying to hide from the presence of the Great Glory. The people of the earth will shake with fear. And you sinners? You will be cursed forever. You will have no peace.

**4** Don't be afraid, you souls of the righteous. Hold onto hope, you who have died walking in righteousness.

**5** Don't grieve because your soul descended to Sheol in sorrow, or because your body in this life didn't get what your goodness deserved. Wait. Wait for the day when sinners are judged, for the day of cursing and punishment.

**6** Even now, when you die, sinners stand over you and say: "They die just like us. So what did being righteous get them?

**7** Look at them — they died in grief and darkness, same as us. What did they have that we didn't? We're all equal now. What are they going to receive? What will they ever see? They're dead. They'll never see light again."

**8** Hear this, sinners: you're perfectly happy eating and drinking, stealing and sinning, stripping people bare, hoarding wealth, living the good life.

**9** Have you looked at the righteous? Have you watched how their life ends — how no violence is found in them, right to the last breath?

**10** And yet they perished. It was as if they had never existed. Their spirits went down to Sheol in suffering.

**11** But now I swear to you, the righteous — by the glory of the Great One, by the glory of his kingdom — I swear: I know the mystery. I have read the heavenly tablets. I have seen the holy books. I have found it written there, inscribed about them.

---

*PNEUMA notes: Vv. 6–7 contain one of the most honest and disturbing passages in the entire Epistle — the sinners are right about the observable facts. The righteous do die in grief. They don't receive justice in this life. Death does look equal. The Enochic response (v. 11) refuses to engage philosophically — instead it appeals to revealed knowledge: I have seen the tablets. The answer is written. Chapter 103 will deliver it.*
